Shape-Constrained Smooth of One Covariate

Source: R/scs.R
scs.Rd

Constructs a smooth function of one covariate constrained to a shape: monotone (shape_increasing(), shape_decreasing()), of constant curvature (shape_convex(), shape_concave()), both (shape_increasing_convex() and the other three combinations), or unimodal or sigmoid (shape_unimodal(), shape_sigmoid()). The term enters the formula of any distribution parameter, like s().

Usage

scs(
  x,
  shape = shape_increasing(),
  smoother = basis7::bspline_smooth(),
  by = NULL,
  by_hyper = c("shared", "level"),
  hyper = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  sparse = NULL
)

Arguments

x

The covariate, a bare name or an expression in the data.

shape

A shape_constraint, by default shape_increasing().

smoother

A basis7 smoother whose basis is a B-spline: basis7::bspline_smooth() (the default) or basis7::pspline_smooth(). Only its basis is used.

by

An optional factor or numeric variable, given as a bare name or an expression in the data, as in s().

by_hyper

With a factor by, whether the levels share one smoothing parameter ("shared", the default) or each has its own ("level"). Under "level" a held value or an id is qualified by the level, hyper = c(lambda.a = 2).

hyper

NULL to estimate the smoothing parameter, or a value at which to hold it, as for s().

id

NULL, or a string shared with other terms whose smoothing parameter is the same, as for s().

label

The term's label; NULL builds scs(<x>) from the call.

sparse

NULL or FALSE: the block is dense.

Value

An unbuilt ScsTerm.

The construction

The covariate is expanded in the B-spline basis of smoother, whose coefficients are written as \(\beta = A\,b(\gamma)\) through the map of the shape (see shape_constraint): cumulative sums of slopes, or of second divided differences, on the Greville abscissae of the basis, each constrained one through the inverse of the shape's link. Every value of the free coefficients \(\gamma\) gives a curve of the shape, so the constraint holds exactly at every iterate of a fit.

The level is removed against the intercept of the model: the first column of \(A\) is dropped and the remaining columns of \(X A\) are centered over the data on which the term is built, so the smooth averages to zero there. The coefficients are therefore \(\gamma_2, \dots, \gamma_K\), named <label>.g1, <label>.g2, and so on.

A shape with a value at a point, value = c(at = a, value = v), removes the level by that value instead: the columns are taken relative to their row at \(a\), and the contribution is \(f(x) = v + (B(x) - B(a))\,A_{-1}\,b_{-1}(\gamma)\). A convex or concave shape with a slope at a point, slope = c(at = a, value = v), has one coefficient fewer, because the slope at the left end is solved from \(f'(a) = v\); the line that this slope contributes is a fixed part of the contribution. See shape_increasing() for when a value other than zero changes the fit.

The penalty

The penalty is the quadratic penalty of first differences of the constrained coordinates of \(\gamma\), under one smoothing parameter lambda selected with the rest of the model. For a convex or concave smooth these are the second divided differences, and the slope at the left end stays free; for a combination the anchored slope is constrained and is the first coordinate of the differences. Under a strong penalty a monotone smooth approaches a straight line, and a convex or concave one the curve whose coefficients have constant second divided differences, which is a parabola in the interior and has a smaller curvature in the end panels of the basis, where the knots are repeated. The penalty of the smoother is not used: the smoother supplies the basis only.

The block

The contribution is nonlinear in \(\gamma\), so the block is the Jacobian \(X_c A_{-1}\,\mathrm{diag}(b'(\gamma))\) at the current coefficients, refreshed by term_refresh(), and term_value() gives the contribution itself. Because \(b\) acts on one coordinate at a time, the derivatives of the block are diagonal in \(\gamma\).

Prediction outside the data

Beyond the ends of the basis the smooth is continued by the straight line with the slope at the end, which preserves the shape.

Positive and bounded functions

The shapes do not include a positive or a bounded function. When a parameter must be positive, or must lie between two values, the range is set by the link of that parameter in the distribution, such as linkfunctions7::log_link() or linkfunctions7::bounded_link(), and s() gives the smooth on the scale of the link. The whole predictor then lies in the range at every iterate. A positive term beside an intercept would not be identified, because a constant moved between the intercept and the term leaves the likelihood unchanged.

Varying the shape by another variable

A factor by gives one constrained curve per level, each with the shape of shape: the block of level \(l\) is the block of one curve multiplied by the indicator of that level, every level is centered over all the rows, as for s(), and the level means come from the factor written in the formula. The coefficients are named <label>.<level>.g1, <label>.<level>.g2, and so on. A value or a slope at a point holds for every level. Under by_hyper = "level" each level has its own smoothing parameter.

A numeric by \(z\) gives a varying-coefficient term \(z\,f(x)\), with the shape on the coefficient \(f\). The term is not centered: the level of \(f\) is the coefficient of \(z\), a free and unpenalized coordinate named <label>.const, so writing \(z\) in the formula as well makes it aliased. With a value at a point the level is fixed by that value instead, and value = c(at = a, value = 0) sets the effect of \(z\) to zero at \(a\). The default label is scs(x):z.

Under a factor by the shape may also differ between the levels: its declared settings (a minimum slope, a location, a peak or a valley, the point and the value of a value or a slope) may be given by level, and its estimated ones (a location that is not given, the left slope of a curvature shape) may be one for every level or one per level, through the arguments mode_by, inflection_by and left_slope_by of the shape (see shape_increasing() and shape_unimodal()). A location chosen by level is searched by statmodels7::statmod() one level at a time from a pilot fit of s(x, by = g) (term_variant_stages()).

Inference

Pointwise intervals from the curvature at the mode cover somewhat less than their nominal level where the curve is flat (about 93 per cent for 95 per cent in simulation); statmodels7::statmod_bootstrap() gives a reading that does not rest on that curvature.

References

Pya, N. and Wood, S. N. (2015). Shape constrained additive models. Statistics and Computing, 25, 543–559.

See also

shape_increasing() and the other shapes, s() for the unconstrained smooth.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(100))
tm <- term_build(scs(x, shape_increasing(), basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 8)), dd)
term_coef_names(tm)
#> [1] "scs(x).g1" "scs(x).g2" "scs(x).g3" "scs(x).g4" "scs(x).g5" "scs(x).g6"
#> [7] "scs(x).g7"

# Every coefficient vector gives an increasing curve.
f <- term_value(tm, coef = rnorm(7))
all(diff(f[order(dd$x)]) >= -1e-12)
#> [1] TRUE
